questions.question: Seven people, X, Y, Z, C, D, E and F, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. E sits fourth to the right of Z. Only two people sit between D and X when counted from the left of D. F sits third to the left of Y. C is an immediate neighbour of Y and X. How many people sit between D and C when counted from the right of D?
questions.questionHtml: Seven people, X, Y, Z, C, D, E and F, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. E sits fourth to the right of Z. Only two people sit between D and X when counted from the left of D. F sits third to the left of Y. C is an immediate neighbour of Y and X. How many people sit between D and C when counted from the right of D?
questions.solution: 2 people sit between D and C when counted from the right of D

questions.question: Each of P, Q, R, S, T, U and V has an exam on a different day of a week starting from Monday and ending on Sunday of the same week. No one has exam before Q. How many people have exams between R and U?

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No hills are mountains. Some mountains are valleys. All valleys are glaciers. Conclusions: (I) No hills are valleys. (II) Some mountains are glaciers.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

No hills are mountains.

Some mountains are valleys.

All valleys are glaciers.

Conclusions:

(I) No hills are valleys.

(II) Some mountains are glaciers.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No hills are valleys → ❌ Cannot be concluded, because there ’ s no direct relation between hills and valleys
II. Some mountains are glaciers → ✅ True, because some mountains are valleys and all valleys are glaciers → some mountains are glaciers
